A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Sitcom-Crafter and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-I. Corresponding material can be matched despite the added subsection and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation evaluations on Replica and InterHuman, quantitative ablations, and experiments incorporating Inter-X.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the system comparisons and appendix ablations in Tables 1-8.

M1.justification: The eight-module system, marker representation, SDF conditioning, canonicalization, losses, and training procedure remain unchanged. New Appendix B.1 explains the existing workflow and discloses initialization details without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same InterHuman, Inter-X, Replica, and synthetic-scene coverage for the same motion-generation tasks. The new workflow example elaborates the existing Figure 2 scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1-3 is unchanged, including ComMDM and InterGen. Newly discussed methods support implementation explanations or future directions; they are not added evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, 11 Replica scenes with 110 plots, frame-rate settings, training budgets, and ablation configurations remain unchanged. No additional evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same canonicalization, conditioning, loss, training-strategy, and data-scale analyses, along with the same qualitative module comparisons and collision failure example. The new workflow diagram is explanatory.

E5.justification: Table 3 specifies 20 evaluation repetitions and 95% confidence intervals in both versions. No new run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added.

E6.justification: Tables 1-8 retain identical numerical entries and rankings, including the proposed method's HSP of 1.6950 in Table 2. Existing qualitative result images are also unchanged; the added figure depicts workflow rather than new results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, SDF construction, canonicalization, and loss formulations are retained. The added explanations introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a plot-driven eight-module system, scene-aware human-human interaction generation, unified motion representation, and augmentation modules.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly qualifies that synthetic scene conditioning improves physical plausibility without significantly enriching interaction diversity or complexity, motivating richer real-world data. Appendices B.2 and C.2 add representation rationale and discuss the efficiency tradeoff between Slerp and potential learned interpolation.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.1 identifies COINS or VPoser for initial-pose generation and explicitly documents sequential module invocation and frame-conditioning handoffs. These are additional disclosures; Appendix D's hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Six references are added concerning body representation, motion interpolation, and large generative models: Kolotouros et al., Zhang et al. (2021), Wang et al., Cohan et al., Rombach et al., and OpenAI. These support localized discussions without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a focused workflow subsection, short explanatory passages, and a limitations paragraph, with corresponding contents and cross-reference updates. Author and publication metadata also change, while the main narrative remains largely verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 7 illustrating command sequencing through generation modules. All existing figure images and table structures are retained, with subsequent figure renumbering, page reflow, and conference headers.

improvement.justification: New Appendix B.1 and Figure 7 make module orchestration clearer and disclose pose initialization. Appendix I more explicitly bounds what scene awareness contributes to interaction diversity. These improve clarity and transparency, while the unchanged methods and experimental evidence make the overall gain limited.
